id: 第四章-终点篇-河童-十七-p1

en: 第四章-终点篇-河童-十七
After I returned from the land of the kappa, for a while I could not bear the smell of human skin.
u.src: 河童国回来之后，有一段时间我无法忍受我们人类的皮肤的气味。

en: Compared with human beings, kappa really are extremely attentive to cleanliness.
u.src: 和人类相比，河童的确十分注意清洁。

en: And once I had grown used to living among kappa, I always felt that human heads were very strange.
u.src: 而且我和河童相处习惯了，总觉得我们人类的脑袋很奇怪。

en: You may not be able to understand this.
u.src: 这件事你可能无法理解。

en: Leaving aside the eyes and mouth, the nose was the thing that frightened me most.
u.src: 先不用说眼睛和嘴，鼻子这东西最让我发怵。

en: Of course, I did everything I could to avoid seeing anyone,
u.src: 当然，我想方设法不去见任何人，

en: but it seems I gradually grew used to being around humans as well,
u.src: 但我好像跟我们人类也慢慢相处习惯了，

en: and after about half a year, I was able to go anywhere.
u.src: 大概过了半年，我就什么地方都能去了。

en: The embarrassing thing was that when I was speaking,
u.src: 难堪的是，我说话的时候，

en: now and then, if I was careless, a phrase of kappa language would slip out.
u.src: 偶尔一不小心就会生活出一句河童话。

en: Will you be staying at home tomorrow?
u.src: “你明天在家待着吗？”
“Qua。”
“你说什么呢？”

ja: にいるということです。
en: Well, what I mean is that I am at home.
u.src: “唔，我的意思是说我在家。”

en: That is roughly what it was like.
u.src: 大概就是这个样子。

en: But after I returned from the land of the kappa, about a year passed,
u.src: 但是自从河童国回来以后，约莫过了一年的时间，

en: and I failed in a certain enterprise...
u.src: 我因为一桩事业失败了……

en: (Just as he had said this much, Dr. S interrupted him and said, "Let us not talk about that for now."
u.src: （他刚讲到这，S博士就打断他说：“先不要谈这个了。”

en: According to the doctor, whenever he spoke of this matter, he caused even the attendants to be at a loss.)
u.src: 据博士所言，他每次谈到这件事，就闹得看护人也手足无措。）

en: Let us not talk about that for now.
u.src: 那就先不谈这个了。

en: Because one of my undertakings had failed, I wanted to return to the land of the kappa again.
u.src: 因为一桩事业失败了，我又想回河童国去。
是的。

en: It was not that I wanted to go there, but that I wanted to go back.
u.src: 不是“想去”，而是“想回去”。

en: To me at that time, the land of the kappa was truly my homeland.
u.src: 在那时候的我看来，河童国才是我的故乡。

en: I ran out of the house, intending to take a train on the Chuo Line.
u.src: 我从家里跑出去，打算去坐中央线火车。

en: Unfortunately, I was caught by the police and was eventually sent to the hospital.
u.src: 不幸的是我被警察抓住了，最后被送进医院。

en: After being suddenly shut up in this hospital, I still kept thinking of the land of the kappas.
u.src: 我突然被关进这个医院，心里还想着河童国。

ja: どうしているのだろうか。
en: How is Doctor Chakka doing now?
u.src: 医生查喀现在如何呢？

ja: んでいるのかもしれない。
en: Perhaps the philosopher Mago is still reading old books beneath a seven-colored glass lantern.
u.src: 哲学家马咯也许仍旧在七彩玻璃灯笼下看古书呢。

en: And above all, my good friend, the student Rappu with the rotting mouth...
u.src: 尤其是我的好朋友——那个烂了嘴巴的学生拉卟……

en: It was an afternoon as gloomy as today, and as I was recalling the past, I almost cried out despite myself.
u.src: 那是一个跟今天一样天气沉郁的下午，我正回忆过去，差点情不自禁叫出声来。

en: Without my knowing when he had come in, the fisherman kappa Bago was standing before me and bowing to me.
u.src: 不知何是进来的，打鱼的河童巴咯站在我面前对我鞠躬示意呢。

en: After I calmed down, I do not remember whether I later cried or laughed, but in any case, speaking kappa language again after so long moved me deeply.
u.src: 我冷静下来了以后——我不记得后来是哭了还是笑了，总之隔了这么长时间再次说河童话，我内心万分感动。

en: Hey, Bago, why did you suddenly come here?
u.src: “嗨，巴咯，你怎么突然来啦？”

en: I heard you were ill, so I came to see you.
u.src: “听说你病了，所以来看看你。”
“你是如何知道的？”

en: I heard it on the radio broadcast.
u.src: “从收音机的广播里得知的。”
巴咯得意地笑着。
“这可不容易呀。”

en: This is really nothing at all.
u.src: “这根本没什么。

en: In a kappa's eyes, whether it is a river or a ditch in Tokyo, it is just like a broad avenue.
u.src: 在河童眼里，无论是东京的河还是沟，就和大马路一样嘛。”

en: Only then did I remember that kappas, like frogs, are amphibious creatures too.
u.src: 我这才记起来，河童和青蛙一样，也是水陆两栖动物。

en: But there is no river around here.
u.src: “可是这附近没有河呀。”

en: I went through the water pipe.
u.src: “我走的自来水管道。

en: Then I opened the fire hydrant...
u.src: 然后打开消火栓……”
“打开消火栓？”
“老爷，您忘记吗？

en: There are craftsmen among the kappa too.
u.src: 河童里面也有工匠呀。”

en: After that, different kappa came to visit me every two or three days.
u.src: 从那之后，每隔两三天就有不同的河童来看我。

en: According to Dr. S's diagnosis, I had early-onset dementia.
u.src: 根据S博士的诊断，我得了早发性痴呆症。

en: But Dr. Chack said that I did not have the illness, and that the ones with early-onset dementia were Dr. S and all of you yourselves.
u.src: 但是查喀医生说，我并没有得这个病，得早发性痴呆症的是S博士和你们自己。

en: Though it may be a little rude of me to say so to you.
u.src: （虽然我这么说可能对你有点失礼。）

en: Even Dr. Chack came to see me, so of course the student Lapp and the philosopher Maro came as well.
u.src: 连医生查喀都来看我了，学生拉卟和哲学家马咯当然也来了。

en: But except for the fisherman Baro, who dared to come by day, the others would appear only at night.
u.src: 但是除了渔夫巴咯敢白天来，其他人都是夜晚才会出现。

en: As soon as it grew dark, especially on moonlit nights, they came in twos and threes, keeping one another company.
u.src: 天只要一黑——尤其月夜，它们就三三两两地搭伴儿一道来了。

en: Last night, by the light of the moon, I even talked with Gar, the owner of the glass company, and with the philosopher Maro.
u.src: 昨天晚上，趁着月夜的光，我还和玻璃公司老板嘎尔以及哲学家马咯一起交谈了呢。

ja: クラバッカは、さらにバイオリンで
en: The musician Kurabakka also played a beautiful piece for me on the violin.
u.src: 音乐家库拉巴喀还用小提琴为我弹奏了一支优美的曲子。

en: Look, do you see that bunch of black lilies on the table over there?
u.src: 喏，看到那边桌子上的一束黑百合花吗？

en: That is the gift Kurabakka brought me last night...
u.src: 那是昨天晚上库拉巴喀给我带来的礼物……

en: (I turned my head and looked at the table.
u.src: （我扭头看了看桌子。

en: Of course, there was not even a trace of a flower on the table.)
u.src: 当然，桌子上连花的影子都没有。）

en: This book was brought to me specially by the philosopher Mago.
u.src: 这本书是哲学家马咯专门给我带过来的。
请你朗诵第一首诗。

en: Oh, you cannot read kappa writing.
u.src: 哦，你看不懂得河童文字。

en: I will read it aloud for you.
u.src: 我读给你听吧。

en: This is one volume from the recently published Complete Works of Tokka.
u.src: 这是最近出版的《托喀全集》里面的一本。

en: (He opens an old telephone directory and reads a poem aloud:)
u.src: （他打开一本旧电话簿，高声读一首诗来：）

en: Among the coconut blossoms and bamboo groves,
u.src: 在椰子花和竹林中，

en: The Buddha entered his rest long ago.
u.src: 佛陀很早就安息了。

en: The first half of Daidoji Shinsuke's life.
u.src: 大导寺信辅的前半生

en: — A landscape painting of a certain state of mind.
u.src: ——某心境风景画
一 本所

en: Daidoji Shinsuke was born near Ekoin Temple in Honjo.
u.src: 大导寺信辅出生在本所的回向院附近。

en: In his memory, there was not a single street that could be called beautiful, nor a single house that could be called fine.
u.src: 在他脑海的记忆力，哪里没有一条称得上美丽的街道，也没有一所称得上漂亮的房子。

en: Especially near his home, there were only carpenters who made underfloor wooden cabinets and bath tubs, cheap sweet shops, secondhand furniture stores, and the like.
u.src: 尤其是在他家附近，都是一些制作地下木柜洗澡桶的木匠、粗点心铺子、旧家具店之类的。

en: The roads in front of these shops were muddy all year round and had never once been dry and clean.
u.src: 这些店铺前面的道路，常年都是泥泞不堪，从来没有干燥清爽过。

en: On top of that, at the end of the road lay the great ditch of Otakegura, a foul-smelling waterway with duckweed floating on its surface all year round.
u.src: 再加上这条道路的尽头就是御竹仓的大水沟——一条河面上飘着浮萍大水沟，常年散发着恶臭气味。

ja: じずにはいられなかった
en: There was no doubt that he could not help feeling oppressed by streets like these.
u.src: 毫无疑问，他对这种街道没办法不感到压抑。

en: But the streets outside Honjo made him feel even more uncomfortable.
u.src: 但是，本所之外的其他街道更让人他觉得不快。

en: From the residential districts of Yamanote to the Shitamachi areas lined with orderly shops handed down from the Edo period, all of them made him feel still more depressed.
u.src: 上从以住宅为主的山手区开始，下到以从江户时代流传下来的、鳞次栉比的整洁店铺为主的下町一代，都让他觉得更加抑郁。

en: Compared with Hongo and Nihonbashi, he loved quiet Honjo more, and loved Ekoin, Komadome Bridge, Yokoami, the drainage canals, Hanoki Baba, and the great ditch of Otakegura even more.
u.src: 和本乡、日本桥相比，他对寂静的本所更加热爱——更热爱回向院、驹止桥、横网、排水渠、榛木马场、御竹仓的大水沟。

en: Rather than love, perhaps it was a feeling closer to sympathy and pity.
u.src: 与其说是热爱，毋宁说是近似同情怜悯的一种情感吧。

en: But even if it was sympathy and pity, so be it!
u.src: 但是，就算是同情怜悯也罢！

en: Even now, thirty years later, only those places still haunt his dreams and hold his soul...
u.src: 一直到三十年后的现在，也只有那些地方让他魂牵梦绕……

en: From the time Shinsuke first became aware of things, he loved the streets of Honjo.
u.src: 从信辅记事儿开始，他就热爱着本所的街道

en: It was a town without even roadside trees, where dust swirled all year round.
u.src: ——一个连街道树木都没有的街道，常年尘土飞扬。

en: Yet it was still the town of Honjo that taught the young Shinsuke the beauty of nature.
u.src: 然而，让年幼的信辅了解到大自然的美丽的也还是本所的街町。

en: He was a boy who grew up eating coarse sweets amid those disorderly streets.
u.src: 他就是在杂乱不堪的街道上，吃着粗点心长大的少年。

en: In fact, the countryside, especially the countryside east of Honjo with rice fields everywhere, held no attraction for a boy like him who had grown up there.
u.src: 其实，乡下——尤其是遍地稻田，在本所东边的乡下，对于他这种乡下长大的少年并没有吸引力。

en: That was because what he saw whenever he lifted his eyes was less the beauty of nature than its ugliness.
u.src: 这是因为他抬眼所能看见的，与其说是自然之美，毋宁说是自然之丑。

en: Although the streets of Honjo had little natural scenery, the wild grasses growing on the roofs and the blue sky and white clouds reflected in puddles all showed a beauty that stirred tender affection.
u.src: 虽然本所的街道没什么自然景色，但是那些长在屋顶上的野草，映在水坑蓝天白云，都呈现出一种让人心生怜爱的美丽。

ja: しさがあったからこそ、
en: It was because of these beauties that he came, without realizing it, to love nature.
u.src: 正是因为这些美丽，他不知不觉得爱上了大自然。

en: But it was not only the streets of Honjo that gradually opened his eyes to the beauty of nature,
u.src: 但是，让他对大自然的美逐渐开拓眼界的，并不只是本所的街道，

en: there were also things he found in books, such as Tokutomi Roka's Nature and Life, which he loved and read several times when he was in elementary school,
u.src: 还有书本上的内容——他小学的时候钟爱阅读过数次的德富芦花的《自然与人生》，

en: and a translated edition of Lubbock's work on the beauty of nature. All of these deeply inspired him.
u.src: 还有拉波克《论自然之美》的翻译版本。这些都让他深受启发。

en: Even so, what influenced his understanding of nature the most was still the town of Honjo.
u.src: 但是，对他认识自然影响最大的仍然是本所的街町。

en: It was a shabby-looking town, whether one looked at its houses, its trees, or even that road.
u.src: 那个不管是房子也好，树木也好，亦或是那条道路，看起来都是十分寒酸的街町。

en: Later, he often took short trips to various places on Honshu.
u.src: 后来，他常常到本州岛的各地短途旅行。

en: But the rugged natural scenery of Kiso made him uneasy, while the graceful scenery of the Seto Inland Sea bored him.
u.src: 但是木曾的粗狂自然风景令他感觉不安，濑户内海优雅的自然风景又令他感觉无聊。

en: Compared with those beautiful and magnificent natural landscapes, he loved shabby scenery more.
u.src: 和那些美丽的、卓越的自然风景相比，他更热爱寒酸的自然风景。

en: He especially loved natural scenery that barely survived amid man-made civilization.
u.src: 尤其热爱那些在人工文明当中苟延残喘的自然风景。

en: Thirty years ago, Honjo still retained much natural beauty, such as the willows along the drainage ditches, the open grounds of Ekoin, and the groves of mixed trees around the Otake storehouses.
u.src: 三十年前，本所还残留着很多许多诸如污水沟的柳树、回向院的广场、御竹仓的杂木树林之类的自然之美。

ja: くことはできなかった
en: He could not go to Nikko or Kamakura the way his friends did.
u.src: 他没办法和他的朋友一样，去日光或者镰仓。

en: But every morning he would go for a walk near his home together with his father.
u.src: 但是，每天早上他都会跟着父亲一道儿在他家附近散步。

en: For Shinsuke at that time, this was the greatest happiness of all.
u.src: 对于当时的信辅来说，这就是最大的幸福。

en: Yet he felt too embarrassed to boast to his friends about this happiness.
u.src: 然而，他不好意思跟朋友得意的讲述这种幸福。

en: One morning, just as the dawn glow was about to fade, he went for a walk with his father to Hyakumokugui, as usual.
u.src: 某个早上，朝霞即将散去，像往常一样他跟着父亲去百木杭散步。

en: Hyakumokugui was the place along the bank of the Okawa where fishermen gathered in the greatest numbers.
u.src: 百木杭是大川岸边钓鱼人最多的地方。

en: But that morning, when he looked up and gazed around, not a single fisherman could be seen.
u.src: 但是，那天早上，抬眼望去，却看不见一个钓鱼人。

en: On the broad riverbank, all he could see were wharf roaches slowly wriggling between the stone walls.
u.src: 宽阔的河岸上，只能看见石垣之间的船虫缓慢蠕动。

ja: りをしていないのかと、
en: He was just about to ask his father why no one was fishing that morning.
u.src: 为什么今天早上没人钓鱼呢，他正想问父亲。

en: But before he could open his mouth, he suddenly understood the answer.
u.src: 但是，他还没来得及开口，忽然就知道答案了。

en: In the rippling water lit by the morning glow, a bald corpse was floating among the tangled wooden stakes, around which foul-smelling water plants and refuse had gathered.
u.src: 在朝霞照耀下的摇晃的水波里，有一具秃头尸体漂浮在杂乱的木桩之间，木桩周围积满了散发臭味的水草和垃圾。

en: That scene at Hyakumokugui on that morning remains vivid in his memory even now.
u.src: ——那天早上百木杭的这一幕，至今仍记忆犹新。

en: The Honjo of thirty years earlier had left many landscapes worth remembering in the sentimental Shinsuke's memory.
u.src: 三十年前的本所，在多愁善感的信辅记忆里，留下了很多值得回忆的风景画。

en: But Hyakumokugui that morning, that one landscape, became the entire psychological shadow that the streets of Honjo cast over Shinsuke's heart.
u.src: 但是，那天早上的百木杭——那张风景画，却成为本所的街町在信辅心中投下的心理阴影的全部！
二 牛乳

en: Shinsuke had never drunk breast milk.
u.src: 信辅没喝过母乳。

en: His mother had always been rather frail, and after giving birth to him, her precious only child, she had no milk at all.
u.src: 母亲原本身体就比较虚弱，生下他这个命根子后，更是一点奶都没有。

ja: うこともできなかった
en: Not only that, but because the family was poor, they could not afford to hire a wet nurse either.
u.src: 不但这样，因为家里穷，也请不起奶妈。

en: So from the time he was born, he grew up entirely on cow's milk.
u.src: 因此，他从出生之后，就是一直靠着喝牛奶长大的。

en: For Shinsuke at that time, this was truly a vexing fate.
u.src: 对于那个时候的信辅来说，这真是一个令人懊恼的命运。

en: He looked down on the milk bottles delivered to the kitchen every morning, and envied his friends who, though they understood nothing else, knew how to drink breast milk.
u.src: 他轻视每天早上送到厨房的牛奶瓶，羡慕那些就算什么都不懂却了解怎么喝母乳的朋友。

en: When he was in elementary school, on some day whose occasion he did not know, his young aunt came to his house, apparently suffering badly because her breasts were swollen with milk.
u.src: 他上小学的时候，不知道是信念还是什么其他日子，年轻的婶婶来到他家，据说是涨奶涨的很痛苦。

en: His aunt tried to express the milk into a brass rinsing cup, but no matter what she did, none would come out.
u.src: 婶婶想把奶水挤在一个黄铜的漱口杯里，但是却无论如何也挤不出来。

en: Frowning, his aunt said to him half in jest, "Little Shin, help your aunt suck the milk out!"
u.src: 婶婶皱着眉头，半开玩笑的跟他说：“小新帮婶婶把奶水吸出来吧！”

en: But having grown up on cow's milk, he had no idea at all how to suck breast milk.
u.src: 但是喝牛奶长大的他，根本不知道怎么吸母乳。

en: Later, his aunt found the daughter from the neighboring carpenter's family and had her help suck at the breasts that had swollen hard with milk.
u.src: 后来，婶婶找到邻居木匠家的女儿，帮忙吸食婶婶涨的发硬的乳房。

en: His aunt's breasts bulged like half-spheres, covered with bluish veins.
u.src: 婶婶的乳房鼓得像半个圆球，上面满是青色静脉。

en: Shinsuke was shy by nature, and even if he had known how to suck milk, he certainly would not have wanted to suck his aunt's milk.
u.src: 信辅生来腼腆，即使他知道怎么吸奶，他也一定不愿意去吸食婶婶的奶水。

en: Even so, he still hated the daughter from the neighboring carpenter's family.
u.src: 虽然这样，他仍然讨厌邻居木匠家的女儿。

en: At the same time, he also hated the aunt who had let the neighboring carpenter's daughter suck her milk.
u.src: 同时，他也讨厌让邻居木匠家的女儿吸奶的深深。

en: This small incident left a very gloomy jealousy in Shinsuke's heart.
u.src: 这样小事在信辅的心中留下了很是阴郁的嫉妒心理。

en: But apart from this incident, perhaps by then his Vita sexualis, literally meaning the life of sexual desire, had already begun to stir...
u.src: 但是，除了这件事之外，可能那时候他的Vita sexualis（直接翻译的意思是性欲的生活）已经蠢蠢欲动了……

en: Shinsuke considered it a terrible disgrace that he had only ever drunk bottled milk and had never drunk his mother's milk.
u.src: 信辅认为自己只喝过瓶装牛奶，但却没喝过母乳这件事是奇耻大辱。

ja: けるつもりはなかった。
en: This was the greatest secret of his life, one he would never reveal to anyone.
u.src: 这是他一生最大的秘密，永远都不会向任何人透露。

en: He also held a certain superstitious notion about this secret.
u.src: 对于这个秘密，他还有某种迷信想法。

en: He was a boy with a very large head but a very thin body.
u.src: 他是个脑袋很大，但是身体很瘦的少年。

en: Not only that, he was shy and timid, the kind of boy who would be frightened even by the gleaming butcher's knife in a meat shop.
u.src: 不仅仅是这样，他不仅容易害羞，而且胆子很小，是一个看见肉铺里明晃晃的屠宰刀都会害怕的少年。

en: On this point, especially on this point, he could be sure that he was nothing like his father, who had fought bravely through the hail of bullets at the Battle of Toba-Fushimi.
u.src: 这一点——尤其是这一点，他可以确认自己完全不像经历过伏见鸟羽战役，在枪林弹雨中勇敢战斗过的父亲。

en: At some point, and for some reason he did not know, he came to believe that he was so unlike his father because he had been raised on cow's milk.
u.src: 不知从何时起，也知是因为什么缘故，他认为自己完全不像父亲是因为喝牛奶长大的缘故。

en: No, he even believed that his physical weakness, too, came from having been raised on cow's milk.
u.src: 不，他还认为自己身体虚弱也是因为喝牛奶长大的缘故。

en: If all of this was caused by drinking cow's milk, then the moment he showed the slightest weakness, his friends would surely expose his secret.
u.src: 如果这一切都是因为喝牛奶所导致的话，那么只要自己稍微示弱，那么他的朋友们就一定会戳穿自己的秘密。

en: So, whenever the time came, he would accept his friends' challenges.
u.src: 所以，不管什么时候，他都会接受朋友们的挑战。

ja: こったことがなかった。
en: Of course, such a challenge had never actually occurred.
u.src: 当然了，这种挑战从来也没发生过。

en: At times, he could leap over the large ditch at O-takegura without using a bamboo pole.
u.src: 时而，他可以不撑竹竿就跃过御竹仓的大水沟。

en: At other times, he could climb the tall ginkgo tree inside Ekoin without using a ladder.
u.src: 时而，他可以不用梯子就爬上回向院内高高的银杏树。

en: Sometimes, he would even get into a fight with one of his friends.
u.src: 时而，他也会跟某个朋友打架。

en: In fact, whenever Shinsuke prepared to leap over the large ditch, he could feel his knees trembling with fear.
u.src: 实际上，当信辅计划跃过大水沟的时候，他都能够感受到自己的膝盖因为恐惧而发抖。

en: Even so, he would always squeeze his eyes shut, summon every bit of strength in his body, and clear the duckweed-covered ditch in a single bound.
u.src: 不过，他总是紧闭双眼，用尽全身力气，一下子就跃过飘着浮萍的大水沟。

en: Moreover, when he climbed the tall ginkgo tree inside Ekoin, or after he had fought with one of his friends, fear and cowardice still assailed the depths of his heart.
u.src: 此外，当他爬上回向院内高高的银杏树时，或者当他和某个朋友打架的是以后，他的内心深处依然内恐惧和胆怯侵袭。

en: Yet every time, he was able to overcome that fear and cowardice with courage.
u.src: 不过，他每次都能勇敢的克服这种恐惧和胆怯。

en: If one wants to say that all this was due to superstition, that is all right too.
u.src: 如果要说这些都是因为迷信也无所谓吧！

en: But it was certainly a Spartan form of self-training.
u.src: 但是，那肯定是斯巴达式的自我训练。

en: This Spartan self-training left a scar on his right knee that would never disappear.
u.src: 这种斯巴达式的自我训练，使得他的右膝盖留下了永远都去不掉的伤痕。

en: Perhaps his character was the same way; even now, Shinsuke clearly remembered the words his father used to scold him: "You are a coward who loves to put on a brave front, and that is no good."
u.src: 也许他的性格也是这样——直到现在，信辅还清楚的记得父亲训斥他的话：“你就是个胆小却爱逞能的人，这样是不好的啊！”

en: Fortunately, however, he gradually freed himself from that superstition.
u.src: 不过，幸运的是他逐渐摆脱了那种迷信。

en: Not only that, he also found facts in Western history that disproved that superstition.
u.src: 不仅仅是这样，他还在西洋历史中发现了反证那种迷信的事实。

ja: くところでは、ローマの
en: It is said that Romulus, the founder of Rome, was actually raised on the milk of a she-wolf.
u.src: 据说罗马建国者罗慕路斯竟然是吃一只母狼的奶水长大的。

en: After that, he no longer brooded over the fact that he had never been fed breast milk.
u.src: 从那以后，他就对没吃过母乳这件事不再耿耿于怀了。

en: No, to be precise, he even felt a faint pride in having been raised on cow's milk.
u.src: 不，准确的说是他甚至对喝牛奶长大这件事感到隐隐的骄傲。

en: Shinsuke remembered that in the spring of the year he had just entered middle school, he went with his somewhat older uncle to the ranch that his uncle ran.
u.src: 信辅记得，他刚上初中的那年春天，他和有些年长的叔父一道儿去叔父经营的牧场。

en: At the time, he strained with all his might just to press the chest of his uniform against the fence,
u.src: 当时他费尽力气才把穿着制服的胸口贴在栅栏上，

en: and fed the hay in his hand to a white cow that had come up in front of him.
u.src: 把手里的干草喂给走到自己面前的白牛吃。

en: The white cow lifted its face and looked at him, then silently lowered its nose to the hay and sniffed it.
u.src: 白牛抬起脸看着他，一声不吭的把鼻子放在干草上闻。

en: When he too raised his head and looked at the cow's face, he found that there seemed to be some feeling in its eyes resembling that of a human being.
u.src: 当他也抬头看牛脸的时候，他发现牛的眼睛里似乎有什么和人类相似的感情。

en: Was it an illusion? It was probably an illusion of his own.
u.src: 是幻想吗？——可能是自己的幻想吧。

en: In his memory, he was leaning against the fence beneath branches blooming with apricot blossoms, and a large white cow was gazing up at her.
u.src: 在他的记忆里，他倚在杏花盛开的树枝下的栅栏上，有一头大白牛仰着头凝视她。

ja: かしんでいるようだった……
en: The cow seemed full of deep feeling, as if overcome with longing...
u.src: 那头牛好像满怀深情，十分怀念一样……
三 贫穷

en: Shinsuke's family could fairly be called very poor.
u.src: 信辅的家里可以说很是贫穷。

en: But their poverty was not the poverty of the lower classes crowded together in a tenement yard,
u.src: 但是，他们的贫穷不是杂居在大杂院里的下层阶级的贫穷，

en: but rather the poverty of the lower middle class, forced to endure greater suffering for the sake of outward respectability.
u.src: 而是为了外表体面而不得不忍受更多的痛苦的中下层阶级的贫穷。

en: His father had once been a government official, but had now retired,
u.src: 他的父亲从前是官吏，如今已经退休，

en: and apart from a small amount of interest on their savings, the four members of the family plus a maid,
u.src: 不包括那一点存款利息在内，他们一家四口加上女佣，

en: five people in all, depended on an annual pension of five hundred yen to get by.
u.src: 五个人，就指望一年五百圆的养老金维持生计。

ja: ねなければならなかった。
en: So they had to practice thrift upon thrift.
u.src: 所以，必须节俭又节俭。

en: They lived in a house with a small garden, but it had only five rooms in all, including the entrance hall.
u.src: 他们住在一栋有小庭院的屋子里，包括玄关在内总共只有五个房间。

en: The people in the household could hardly ever put on a new piece of clothing.
u.src: 家里人几乎很难穿上一件新衣服。

en: Every night his father took as his pleasure a single cup of rough liquor, the sort of drink one could not serve in company.
u.src: 父亲每晚总是以喝一杯粗酒——一种拿不到台面上的酒——当做消遣。

en: His mother, too, would throw a haori over her kimono to hide the patched sash underneath.
u.src: 母亲也以外面披上和服外褂来掩藏里面布满补丁的腰带。

en: As for Shinsuke, even now he remembered that desk with its smell of paint.
u.src: 而信辅，他直到如今都记得那张带着油漆臭味的书桌。

en: The desk was secondhand, with green woolen cloth pasted over its top,
u.src: 书桌是中古货，桌面上贴着绿色的绒布，

en: and the drawer pulls shone with a silvery metallic gleam, so that at first glance it looked rather pretty.
u.src: 抽屉的拉把手闪着银色的金属光泽，猛一看你还挺漂亮的。

en: In reality, the cloth was very thin, and the drawers were hard to pull open.
u.src: 实际上，绒布很薄，抽屉也很难拉开。

en: Rather than calling it his desk, it would be better to call it the symbol of his family.
u.src: 与其说这是他的书桌，毋宁说这是他家的象征。

en: It symbolized the still more painful life his family led for the sake of preserving appearances...
u.src: 象征着他家那种为了顾及体面而过的更加痛苦的生活……

en: Shinsuke felt a deep hatred for this kind of poverty.
u.src: 信辅对这种贫穷有深深的憎恨。

en: No, even now that hatred still remained in his heart and had not faded away.
u.src: 不，直到现在这种憎恨还留在他心里未曾消散。

en: He had no money to buy books, no money to attend summer school, and no money to buy a new overcoat.
u.src: 他没钱买书，没钱参加暑期学校，没钱买新大衣。

en: But his classmates had all of these things.
u.src: 但是他的同学们都拥有这一切。

en: He envied them, and at times he was even jealous of them.
u.src: 他羡慕他们，偶尔还会嫉妒他们。

en: But he would certainly never admit to this envy and jealousy, because he looked down on those classmates who had no ability.
u.src: 但是，他肯定不会承认这种羡慕和嫉妒的，因为他瞧不起那些没本事的同学。

en: However, his hatred of poverty had not changed in the slightest.
u.src: 不过，对于贫穷的这种憎恨，并没有丝毫改变。

en: The old tatami mats, the dim light, and the mottled, peeling traces of ivy on the paper doors,
u.src: 陈旧的榻榻米、昏暗的灯光、纸门上斑驳脱落的常春藤话貌，

en: everything that represented the shabby state of the house filled him with hatred.
u.src: 这一切代表着家里寒酸的样子都使他感到憎恨。

ja: まだましなほうだった。
en: But that was still the better part of it.
u.src: 不过，这还算好的。

en: Because of that shabby life, he even hated his own parents.
u.src: 他甚至因为寒酸的生活，憎恨自己的父母。

en: Especially his bald father, who was even shorter than he was.
u.src: 尤其是那个比他还矮的秃头父亲。

en: His father often came to the school to attend guarantor meetings, and Shinsuke felt ashamed when his father appeared before his classmates.
u.src: 父亲常常来学校参加保证人会议，信辅对出现在同学面前的父亲感觉羞耻。

en: At the same time, he felt ashamed of the inferiority complex that made him look down on his own father.
u.src: 与此同时，他对于自己瞧不起自己的亲生父亲的这种自卑心里感觉羞耻。

en: He once wrote a passage of No Self Deception Diary in imitation of Kunikida Doppo, and the manuscript paper bearing those words has now yellowed—
u.src: 他模仿国木独步写了一段《不自欺记》，如今写着这段话的稿纸已经泛黄——

en: Can I not love my parents?
u.src: “我不能爱我的父母吗？

en: No, it is not that I cannot love them.
u.src: 不是的，不是不能爱。

en: Although I love my father as a person, I do not love my parents' appearance.
u.src: 我虽然爱父亲的人，但是却不爱父母的样貌。

en: Judging people by their looks is a disgrace for a gentleman.
u.src: 以貌取人，对君子来说是耻辱。

en: How much more so when it is my father's appearance?
u.src: 更何况父亲的外貌呢？

en: And yet, no matter what, I still cannot love my parents' appearance.
u.src: 可是，无论如何，我还是无法爱父母的外貌。”

en: Yet there was something he hated even more than a shabby life: the hypocrisy born of poverty.
u.src: 然而，还有比寒酸的生活更让他憎恨的事，那就是贫穷所致的虚伪。

en: His mother would put cakes in a box from Fugetsudo and send them to relatives,
u.src: 母亲用“风月堂”的盒子装蛋糕送亲戚，

en: but what was inside was not Fugetsudo wagashi at all; it was honey cake from a nearby sweet shop!
u.src: 但是那里面装的根本就不是“风月堂”的和菓子，而是附近点心铺的蜂蜜蛋糕啊！

en: His father was the same, always teaching everyone to be frugal and martial in spirit.
u.src: 父亲也是如此，他总是教育大家“勤俭尚武”。

en: But when his father spoke of moral instruction, there was only one old copy of Yupian; anything else, even a Chinese-Japanese dictionary, counted as luxurious and weak!
u.src: 但是，倘若父亲要提到训诫的话，唯有一本陈旧的《玉篇》，除此之外就连《汉和辞典》也算是“奢侈文弱”！

en: Nor was that all: Shinsuke himself knew very well how to lie, and his skill at lying was no worse than his parents'.
u.src: 不仅仅是这样，信辅自己也很懂得说谎，而且说谎的本事并不逊于他的父母。

en: His monthly allowance was fifty sen, and if he could get any extra spending money, even a single sen more, he would use it to buy the books and magazines he liked.
u.src: 他每个月的零用钱是五十钱，倘若能够多弄到零花钱，即使只多一分钱，他也会拿去买喜欢的图书和杂志。

en: For that purpose he would lie, saying that he had lost the money!
u.src: 他会为此撒谎，说钱弄丢啦！

en: He needed to buy a notebook!
u.src: 需要买笔记本啦！

en: He needed to pay class fees!
u.src: 需要缴纳班费啦！

en: In short, he used every excuse he could devise to cheat money out of his parents.
u.src: ——总而言之，想方设法用一切借口，骗父母的钱。

en: Even so, there were times when the money was still not enough, and he had no choice but to do everything he could to please his parents so that he could get next month's allowance early.
u.src: 哪怕是这样，钱还是有不够用的时候，他只能使出浑身解数博得父母的欢心，以便早点拿到下个月的零花钱。

en: What he liked most was winning the favor of his old mother, who doted on him.
u.src: 他最喜欢博取宠爱他的老母亲的欢心。

ja: というわけではなかった
en: Of course, whether he lied himself or his parents lied, it was not all pleasant for him.
u.src: 当然，无论是他自己说谎，还是父母说谎，对他来说不都是愉快的是行情。

en: Nevertheless, he went on lying as ever, lying boldly and cunningly.
u.src: 不过，他还是一如既往地说谎，大胆而狡诈的撒谎。

en: Thus lying was, for him, more specially important than anything else, and from it he could feel a morbid pleasure, a pleasure like having killed something.
u.src: 因此撒谎对他来说，是比什么都特别重要的事，他还能因此感到病态的愉悦——一种好似杀死什么一样的愉悦。

en: In this point alone, he was especially like a delinquent boy.
u.src: 唯有在这一点上，他特别像个无良少年。

en: In Notes on Not Deceiving Oneself, he once wrote the following passage:
u.src: 他在《不自欺记》里写过这么一段——

en: Doppo says one loves for the sake of love; I say one hates for the sake of hatred.
u.src: “独步说为恋爱而恋爱，我说为憎恨而憎恨。

en: Hatred that hates hatred of poverty, hatred that hates hatred of hypocrisy, hatred that hates hatred of everything...
u.src: 憎恨对贫穷的憎恨，憎恨对虚伪的憎恨，憎恨对一切的憎恨……”

en: This was Shinsuke's true feeling: at some point, he had begun to hate his own hatred of poverty.
u.src: 这就是信辅的真心，不知从何时起，他开始憎恨自己对贫穷的憎恨。

en: Until he was twenty, he was constantly troubled by this double hatred.
u.src: 二十岁之前，他一直被这种双重憎恨所困扰。

ja: なかったわけではない。
en: And yet, it was not as though he had no happiness at all.
u.src: 然而，他也不是一点幸福都没有。

en: In every examination, his grades placed him third or fourth.
u.src: 每次考试成绩都能名列第三、第四名。

en: There was also a handsome boy in a lower grade who showed him kindness of his own accord.
u.src: 还有低年级的美少年，主动对他示好。

en: But these were no more than a little sunlight breaking through a cloudy sky.
u.src: 但是，这些不过是云天里露出的一点阳光罢了。

en: Hatred, heavier than any other feeling, lingered in his heart.
u.src: 憎恨比一切感情都更加沉重的在他心头徘徊。

en: Nor was that all: at some point, hatred had left an indelible mark on his heart.
u.src: 不仅仅是这样，不知从何时开始，憎恨在他心里留下了不可磨灭的印记。

en: Even after escaping poverty, he still hated poverty.
u.src: 即使是摆脱贫穷之后，他依然憎恨贫穷。

en: At the same time, he hated luxury just as much as he hated poverty.
u.src: 与此同时，他憎恨奢侈，就像憎恨贫穷一样。

en: His hatred of luxury arose from the imprint of lower-middle-class poverty.
u.src: 他对奢侈的憎恨，就源于对中下层阶级贫穷的印记。

en: Or rather, it was the sole mark left by lower-middle-class poverty.
u.src: 亦或是说，是对中下层阶级贫穷的唯一印记。

en: Even now, he could still feel that hatred in his heart.
u.src: 时至今日，他仍然能够感受到心头的那种憎恨。

en: It was the fear of the petty bourgeois middle class, forced to be constantly ready to fight against poverty...
u.src: 那是不得不时刻准备和贫穷战斗的Petty Bourgeois中产阶级的到的恐惧……

en: In the autumn of the year he graduated from university, Shinsuke went to visit a friend who was then studying law.
u.src: 信辅在大学毕业的那年秋天，去探望当时正在读法律系的朋友。

en: They talked in an eight-tatami guest room where both the walls and the paper sliding doors were quite old.
u.src: 他们在一个墙壁和纸门都很陈旧的八张榻榻米大的客室聊天。

en: An old man of about sixty suddenly peered out from behind the paper sliding door.
u.src: 一个约莫六十岁的老人偶从纸门后方探出一张脸来。

en: From the old man's face, Shinsuke could tell that he was a retired official who had spent many years drinking heavily.
u.src: 信辅在这个老人的脸上看出，那是一个常年酗酒的退休官吏。
“这位是我的父亲。”

en: His friend briefly introduced the old man.
u.src: 他的朋友简单的介绍了这位老人。

ja: ここにあらずといった
en: The old man did indeed wear an arrogant expression, and listened absentmindedly to Shinsuke's greeting.
u.src: 老人的确面带傲气，心不在焉的听信辅的问候。

en: Then, before the old man turned to leave, he said to Shinsuke:
u.src: 然后，在老人转身离开之前，他对信辅说：
“请慢慢聊吧！
那边有椅子。”

en: In the dim corridor there were indeed two armchairs set side by side.
u.src: 在昏暗的廊下的确有两张带扶手的椅子并排放着。

en: However, those two chairs had very high backs, their red cushions had faded, and they were probably old chairs from fifty years earlier.
u.src: 不过，那两张椅子的椅背很高、红色的软垫已经褪色，大概是五十年前的老旧椅子。

en: In those two chairs, Shinsuke saw the impoverished life of the entire lower-middle class.
u.src: 信辅从这两张椅子里看到了整个中下层阶级的贫穷生活。

en: At the same time, he could also see that his friend, like him, felt ashamed to have such a father.
u.src: 与此同时，他也看得出来他的朋友和他一样，为有这样的父亲感觉羞愧。

en: This incident left a deep impression in his memory.
u.src: 这件事情在他记忆里留下了深刻的印象。

en: From then on, these thoughts cast even more confused shadows in his heart.
u.src: 这些思想从此在他心里投下了更多杂乱的阴影。

en: In short, he was indeed the son of a retired official.
u.src: 总而言之，他的确是一个退休官吏的儿子。

en: Compared with the poverty of the lower class, he had to endure the false poverty of the lower-middle class.
u.src: 和下层阶级的贫穷相比，他不得不忍受虚伪的中下层阶级贫穷。
四 学校

en: In Shinsuke's memory, school life was entirely gloomy.
u.src: 学校生活在信辅的记忆里都是阴暗的。

en: During his university years, apart from a few courses that did not require taking notes, he had no interest in any of the others.
u.src: 大学时期，除了几门不用做笔记的课程之外，他对其他任何课程都不感兴趣。

en: For him, studying step by step from middle school to high school, and from high school to university, was merely a way of saving himself from poverty.
u.src: 从初中到高中，从高中到大学，一级一级的读书，对他来说只是摆脱贫穷的自我救赎方法罢了。

en: Originally, during his middle school days, Shinsuke did not acknowledge this fact, or at least had never acknowledged it clearly.
u.src: 本来信辅在中学时代并不认可这个事实，至少没有明确认可过。

en: But from middle school onward, poverty began to settle over Shinsuke's heart like a dark cloud.
u.src: 可是，从初中开始，贫穷像乌云一样开始盘踞在信辅的心头。

en: In high school and university, Shinsuke wanted several times to drop out.
u.src: 在高中和大学时，信辅数次想要辍学。

en: But the threat of poverty foretold a bleak future, and so he always gave up the idea of leaving school quite easily.
u.src: 但是，贫穷的威胁正预见着灰暗的未来，因此他总是轻易放弃辍学的打算。

en: Without question, he hated school, and he especially hated middle school, with all its countless rules.
u.src: 毫无疑问，他憎恨学校，特别憎恨规矩特别多的初中。

en: How unbearably shrill and mournful was the bugle from the school gatehouse!
u.src: 学校门房的喇叭声无比凄厉啊！

en: How unbearably melancholy, too, were the leafy poplars on the playground!
u.src: 操场上枝繁叶茂的白杨树也无比忧郁啊！

en: What Shinsuke learned at school was nothing but useless scraps of knowledge, such as dates in European history, chemical equations without experiments, and the population of some European city.
u.src: 信辅在学校学到的都是一些无用的小知识，诸如欧洲历史的时间、没有实验的化学方程式、欧洲某城市的人口数量，等等。

en: As long as one paid even a little attention, learning such things was not necessarily painful.
u.src: 只要略微用点心，学习这些知识不一定痛苦。

en: Yet in fact, trying to forget these useless scraps of knowledge was by no means simple.
u.src: 然而，事实上，想忘掉这些无用的小知识却并不简单。

en: In Dostoevsky's Notes from a Dead House, it is written: "If prisoners were forced to perform useless labor, for example:
u.src: 杜思妥耶夫斯基的《死屋手记》里写过：“倘若强迫囚犯做无用的劳务，比如：

en: pouring the water from the first bucket into the second bucket, then pouring the water from the second bucket back into the first, the prisoners would rather kill themselves."
u.src: 把第一桶水倒进第二个桶里，再把第二桶水倒回第一个桶里，囚犯就会宁愿自杀。”

en: In the gloomy school buildings, beneath the swaying poplars, Shinsuke felt the mental anguish that prisoners feel.
u.src: 在灰暗的校舍里，在摇曳的白杨树下，信辅感受到了囚犯所感受的精神痛苦。
不仅仅是这样……

en: Not only that, the people he hated most were also his middle school teachers.
u.src: 不仅仅是这样，他最憎恨的也是初中时候的老师。

en: As ordinary people, those teachers surely were not bad people.
u.src: 身为一个普通人的老师肯定不是个坏人。

en: But because they bore an educational responsibility, and especially because they had the power to punish students, they naturally became tyrants.
u.src: 但是，由于他们承担“教育责任”——尤其是有权利处罚学生，自然他们就会成为暴君。

en: They stopped at nothing to instill their own prejudices into the hearts of their students.
u.src: 他们为了将自己的偏见灌输到学生里心里，不择手段。

en: One of them, an English teacher nicknamed Daruma, often punished Shinsuke on the grounds that he was arrogant.
u.src: 其中一个外号叫“达摩”的英语老师，常常以信辅“傲慢”的理由惩罚他。

en: But the reason Shinsuke was considered arrogant was, astonishingly, that he read books by Kunikida Doppo and Tayama Katai.
u.src: 但是，信辅之所以被认为“傲慢”，竟然是因为他阅读国木田独步和田山花袋的书。

en: There was also a Japanese language teacher with an artificial left eye who looked down on Shinsuke because he disliked martial arts and athletic competitions.
u.src: 还有一个左眼装的是义眼的国语老师，以信辅不喜欢武术和运动比赛的理由而看不起他。

en: Several times he mocked Shinsuke, saying, Are you a woman?
u.src: 曾经数次讽刺信辅：“你是个女人吗？”

en: Shinsuke asked him back, Are you a man?
u.src: 信辅反问他：“你是个男人吗？”

en: Naturally, the teacher punished him for such an arrogant attitude.
u.src: 老师对他这种傲慢的态度当然会惩罚。

en: As for the rest, one need only reread that book, A Record of Not Deceiving Myself, to know that the humiliations he suffered were beyond counting.
u.src: 其他事情，只要重新读一遍那本《不自欺记》，就能知道他所遭受的屈辱不胜其数。

en: Shinsuke had a strong sense of pride, and to preserve his dignity he had no choice but to resist such humiliation.
u.src: 信辅自尊心很强，为了争一口气，不得不反抗这种屈辱。

en: If he had not resisted in this way, he might have come to despise himself like a delinquent youth.
u.src: 如果他不如此反抗的话，他也许会像不良少年般不屑自己。

en: His path of self-strengthening can undoubtedly be found in A Record of Not Deceiving Myself.
u.src: 他的自强之道，无疑可以在《不自欺记》中找到——

en: Although I have been burdened with many infamous labels, there are three underlying reasons for this.
u.src: 我虽然蒙上诸多恶名，深究其中的原因有三个。

en: First, he was bookish and frail.
u.src: 其一，文弱。

en: A so-called bookish and frail person is someone who values spiritual strength more than physical strength.
u.src: 所谓文弱的人，也就是重视精神力量胜过肉体力量。
其二，轻浮。

en: A so-called frivolous person is one who loves perfect things beyond mere utility.
u.src: 所谓轻浮的人，也就是钟爱功利之外的完美事物。
其三，傲慢。

en: A so-called arrogant person is also someone who does not casually bend his own convictions in front of others.
u.src: 所谓傲慢的人，也就是在他人不前不妄屈自己所信。

ja: いじめたわけではなかった
en: However, not all of the teachers bullied him.
u.src: 然而，也不是所有的老师都欺负他。

en: Among them, there were also teachers who invited Shinsuke to family tea gatherings, and teachers who lent him English novels.
u.src: 他们之中，也曾有老师招待信辅参加家庭茶会，也有老师借给他英文小说。

en: He vividly remembered an English translation of A Sportsman's Sketches that he borrowed when graduating from fourth year, and he read it through with great delight.
u.src: 他对四年级毕业时借来的一本《猎人笔记》的英译本记忆犹新，满心欢心的阅读完。

en: But the burden of educational responsibility often interfered with warm relations between teachers and ordinary people.
u.src: 但是，由于承担“教育责任”常常影响老师和普通人亲切来往。

en: This was because, while accepting their kindness, there also lurked a certain humble flattery and currying of favor toward their authority.
u.src: 这是因为在接受他们示好的同时，还潜藏着某种对他们权力的卑微的奉承和讨好。

en: Or else there lurked the ugly spectacle of flattering their homosexual tendencies.
u.src: 要不然，就是潜藏着对他们同性恋倾向的奉承丑态。

en: Whenever Shinsuke appeared before them, he always felt blocked and at a loss.
u.src: 信辅每次在他们面前出现的时候，总是感到受阻无所。

en: Not only that, sometimes he would go and take cigarettes without reserve, or show off about small things such as having watched a play while standing.
u.src: 不仅仅是这样，有时候还会不拘束的去拿香烟，或者显摆自己站着看戏的一些小事。

en: Naturally, they interpreted this behavior as arrogance.
u.src: 他们自然把这种行为解释成傲慢。

en: There was nothing especially wrong with that interpretation either.
u.src: 这种解释也没什么问题。

en: After all, he was never a likable student to begin with.
u.src: 本来他就不是个招人喜欢的学生。

en: Judging from an old photograph kept at the bottom of a box, at that time he was a sickly boy with a large head out of proportion to his body, but with bright, piercing eyes.
u.src: 从放在箱子底部的旧照片来看，当时是他头很大，是个头和身体很不相称，但眼睛炯炯有神的病弱少年。

en: This pale, sickly boy was always asking tricky questions and taking pleasure in embarrassing his teachers.
u.src: 这个气色不好的病弱少年总是不停的提出刁钻问题，以为难老师为乐。

en: On every exam, Shinsuke was able to get high marks.
u.src: 每次考试成绩，信辅都能得到高分。

en: But for conduct, he never received more than six points, the passing mark.
u.src: 但是，操行成绩却都没得过六分（及格分）以上。

en: Whenever he saw the Arabic numeral 6, he could almost hear the teachers sneering in the staff room.
u.src: 他每次看到6这个阿拉伯数字，都几乎能听到老师们在办公室的冷笑声。

en: In fact, it was true that the teachers used his conduct score as a shield and kept mocking him.
u.src: 事实上，老师用操行分数当盾牌，老嘲笑他也是确实存在的。

en: Because of that six, his overall marks could never place him among the top three.
u.src: 他的总成绩因为这个六分，总也无法名列前三。

en: He hated this act of retaliation, and he hated the teachers who carried it out.
u.src: 他憎恨这种报复行为，也憎恨这种报复行为的老师。

en: By now, no, up to this very moment, he had gradually forgotten the hatred he felt then.
u.src: 到现在——不，直到现在，他已经渐渐忘记当时的这种憎恨。

en: Still, a nightmare is not necessarily a misfortune.
u.src: 不过，噩梦不一定就是不幸。

en: At least because of it, he developed a temperament capable of enduring loneliness.
u.src: 至少他因此养成了忍受孤独的性情。

ja: しかったかもしれない。
en: Otherwise, the suffering he experienced in the latter half of his life might have been even more painful than it was.
u.src: 不然他下半辈子所经历的痛苦可能比现在更加痛苦。

en: As if in a dream, he became a writer and published several books.
u.src: 他像做梦一样成了一个作家，出版了几本书。

en: Yet all he gained was desolation and loneliness.
u.src: 然而，他所得到的只有落寞和孤独。

en: Now that he had grown used to loneliness, or rather, now that there was no better way than to grow used to loneliness,
u.src: 已经习惯孤独的今天——或者说除了习惯孤独之外，没有更好的办法的今天，

en: looking back over the past twenty years, the middle school building that had once filled him with hatred and pain
u.src: 回忆过去的二十年，那曾经让他憎恨和痛苦的中学校舍，

en: seemed, rather, to be already shining in a beautiful rose-colored morning light.
u.src: 不如说已经照耀在一片美丽蔷薇色的晨光中了。

en: Only the leafy poplars on the playground remained, with a lonely wind blowing through them...
u.src: 只剩下操场上枝繁叶茂的白杨树，有寂寥的风吹过……
五 书籍

en: From elementary school onward, Shinsuke loved reading books.
u.src: 信辅从小学开始，就很喜欢阅读图书。

en: The Imperial Library edition of Water Margin at the bottom of his father's bookcase was the source that awakened his interest in reading.
u.src: 他父亲书箱底部的那本帝国文库本《水浒传》是引起他阅读兴趣的源头。

en: This frail elementary school boy, with only his large head standing out, read Water Margin over and over by dim lamplight.
u.src: 这个只有一个大脑袋的瘦弱小学生，靠着昏暗的灯光，读了很多遍《水浒传》。

en: Nor was that all; even after he closed the book, his mind kept picturing the banner of carrying out justice on Heaven's behalf,
u.src: 不仅仅是这样，即使他合上书本，脑子里仍然始终想象替天行道的旗帜，

en: the tiger on Jingyang Ridge, and the human legs that Zhang Qing the Vegetable Gardener had hung from the rafters.
u.src: 景阳冈山上的老虎，菜园子张青在屋梁上挂着的人腿。

en: Were all these things only imagination? Yet this imagination was more real than reality itself.
u.src: 这些都是想象吗？——可是这种想象比现实还要真实。

en: More than once, wooden sword in hand, he fought in the yard where dried vegetables hung against characters from Water Margin,
u.src: 他曾经数次手里拿着木剑，在挂着晒干菜的院子里和《水浒传》书中里人物——

en: thrashing One Zhangqing Hu Sanniang and the Flowery Monk Lu Zhishen soundly.
u.src: 一丈青扈三娘、花和尚鲁智深，打个落花流水。

en: For more than thirty years, this passion had sustained him deep in his heart.
u.src: 三十多年以来，这种激情一直在他心头支持着他。

en: He remembered spending many nights awake until dawn, reading books without sleeping.
u.src: 他记得自己曾经很多天彻夜不眠的阅读书籍。

ja: いや、それだけではない。
en: No, it was more than that: whether he was sitting at his desk, riding in a vehicle, or even going to the toilet,
u.src: 不，不仅仅是这样，不管是坐在书桌前、车上，还是上厕所的时候——

en: at times he would even sink into reading while he was walking.
u.src: 偶尔甚至连走路的时候也会沉溺在阅读之中。

en: After Water Margin, he never picked up a wooden sword again.
u.src: 从《水浒传》之后，他没再拿起过木剑。

en: Yet many times he had laughed and cried over the events in that book.
u.src: 然而，他曾经多次因为那本书里的情节哭哭笑笑。

en: In other words, he had already entered the self-forgetting state of complete identification.
u.src: 换言之，已经进入了“完全移情”的忘我境界。

en: He himself had almost become one of the people in the book.
u.src: 就连他自己也简直成了书里的人物了。

en: At one time, like the Buddha of India, he had been reborn countless times.
u.src: 曾经，他就像天竺佛祖一样转世了无数次。

ja: はイワン・カラマーゾフ、ハムレット、
ドン・フアン、メフィスト、
en: He became Ivan Karamazov, Hamlet, Prince Andrei, Don Juan, Mephistopheles, Reynard the Fox, and many others.
u.src: 他变成了伊凡·卡拉马佐夫、哈姆雷特、安德烈公爵、唐璜、梅菲斯特、列那狐等等。

en: And this was not a momentary loss of self through identification.
u.src: ——并且，这不是一时的移情忘我。

en: One afternoon in late autumn, wanting to ask for a little spending money, he visited his elderly uncle.
u.src: 在一个晚秋的中午之后，因为想要讨要一些零花钱，他去拜访上了年纪的叔父。

en: Because his uncle was from Hagi in Choshu, he deliberately kept praising before him the outstanding achievements of the Meiji Restoration,
u.src: 叔父是长州萩人，他故意在叔父不停的夸奖明治维新的卓越成绩，

en: and went on praising Choshu-born figures from Murata Seifu to Yamagata Aritomo without pause.
u.src: 从村田清风，到山县有朋等长州出身的人，都夸赞个不停。

en: Yet he himself also felt that this pale, frail high school student filled with false enthusiasm
u.src: 然而，他自己也觉得这个充满虚伪激情、神色苍白的文弱高中生，

ja: きジュリアン・ソレルだった。
en: was not so much Daidoji Shinsuke of that time as the young Julien Sorel, the protagonist of The Red and the Black.
u.src: 与其说是当时的大导寺信辅，毋宁说是《红与黑》里的主人公于——年轻的连·索海尔。

en: Such was Shinsuke: everything he knew, he had learned from books.
u.src: 这样的信辅，所有的事情都是从书里学来的。

ja: されなかったものはない。
en: At the very least, one could say there was not a single thing in him that had not been inspired by books.
u.src: 至少可以说，我没有任何一件事不是从书本里得到启发的。

en: In fact, he was the sort of person who ignored passersby in the street in order to think about life.
u.src: 事实上，他是一个为了思考人生而无视街头行人的人。

en: Or rather, instead of observing passersby, he preferred to think about the lives found in books.
u.src: 或者说，与观察行人相比，他更愿意思考书本里的人生。

en: Perhaps one might say this was his indirect way of understanding life.
u.src: 或者可以说这是他理解人生的曲线手段吧！

en: Yet to him, the passersby in the street were nothing more than ordinary passersby.
u.src: 可是，对于他来说，街头行人不过是普通行人罢了。

en: To understand their lives, to understand their love, their hatred, and their vanity, he had only one method: reading books.
u.src: 他为了理解他们的人生——理解他们的爱，理解他们的憎恨，理解他们的虚荣心，唯有读书一个方法。

en: Books, especially the novels and plays published in fin-de-siecle Europe, finally opened scene after scene of human comedy in his austere heart.
u.src: 书籍，尤其是世纪末欧洲出版的小说和戏剧，终于在他冷峻的心里，开启了一幕幕人间喜剧。

en: No, rather, they showed him his own soul, which made no distinction between good and evil,
u.src: 不，毋宁说是让他看到了自己不分善恶的灵魂，

en: And not only his own life; through them he also saw the natural beauty of the streets of Honjo.
u.src: 不仅限于他自己的人生，他也因此看到了本所街町的自然之美。

en: But what made his eyes for nature sharper was still the inspiration of a few favorite books, especially the haikai of the Genroku era.
u.src: 但是，让他观看自然的眼睛更加锐利的依然是靠几本喜欢的书的启发——尤其是元禄时代的绯谐。

en: It was precisely because he had read those haiku, such as "Viewing the mountains near the capital," "In the turmeric fields, autumn is high and the air is clear," and "A blue heron flies crying through the dark night,"
u.src: 正是因为他读了那些绯句，诸如，“近京城观山形”、“郁金田秋高气爽”、“黑夜飞过苍鹭啼”等，

en: That he discovered in the streets of Honjo a natural beauty he had never seen there before.
u.src: 他才发现本所街町前所未有的自然之美。

en: For Shinsuke, this process of going "from books to reality" was truth itself.
u.src: 这种从“书籍到现实”的过程，对信辅来说就是真理。

en: In the course of his own half life, he too had felt affection for several women.
u.src: 他在自己的半生中也曾对几个女子有过爱慕之情。

en: But this did not teach him the beauty of women outside of books.
u.src: 但这并没让他了解到书本之外的女性之美。

ja: ゴーティエ、バルザック、トルスタンの
en: Only through the descriptions of Gautier, Balzac, and Tolstoy did Shinsuke come to know the beauty of a woman's "ears translucent in the sunlight" and "the shadow of eyelashes falling on the cheek."
u.src: 从戈蒂耶、巴尔扎克、托尔斯坦的梳理，信辅才了解到女性“穿透阳光的耳朵”和“落在脸颊上的睫毛的剪影”的美好。

ja: やはりこれらのものだった。
en: Even now, these were still the forms of feminine beauty that Shinsuke admired.
u.src: 时至今日，信辅欣赏的女性之美还是这些。

ja: らなかったかもしれない。
en: Had he not learned these things from books, he might have known only that women were female.
u.src: 如果不是从书本里学到了这些的话，可能他只能知道女性就是雌性吧。

en: However, Shinsuke was very poor and could not freely buy the books he wanted to read.
u.src: 可是，信辅很是贫穷，没办法随心所欲的买自己想要阅读的书。

en: So he found ways to solve this difficult problem: first, the library; second, rental bookshops; and third, the kind of frugality that made other people laugh at him.
u.src: 因此，他想办法来解决这个难题，第一是图书馆，第二是租书店，第三是让别人讥讽的省吃俭用。

en: He always remembered clearly the rental bookshop facing the large drainage ditch, the kindly old woman in the shop, and her side work making ornamental hairpins.
u.src: 他始终清楚的记得面对大水沟的租书店，租书店里的慈祥老婆婆，还有老婆婆做簪花的副业。

en: The old woman thought this young master, who had just started elementary school, was innocent.
u.src: 老婆婆认为这个刚上小学的“小少爷”是单纯的。

ja: ちゃん」はいつのまにか
en: But before he knew it, this young master had learned how to pretend to be looking for books while actually reading them on the sly.
u.src: 但是，这个“小少爷”却在不知不觉中学会了假装在找书，实际是在偷看书的办法。

en: He also clearly remembered Jinbocho twenty years earlier, when secondhand bookshops filled the whole street and sunlight often shone on the Kudan slope behind their roofs.
u.src: 他也清楚的记得，二十年前的神保町，旧书店布满整条街，阳光常常照耀在旧书店屋顶后面的九段斜坡。

en: Needless to say, Jinbocho at that time had no streetcars, and not even horse-drawn carriages.
u.src: 不必多说，当时的神保町不仅没有电车，就连马车也没有。

en: He, a twelve-year-old elementary school student, would tuck his lunch and notebook under his arm and hurry back and forth along that street again and again on his way to the Ohashi Library.
u.src: 他，一个十二岁的小学生为了去大桥图书馆，总是在胳膊下夹着便当和笔记本，频繁的往返奔走在那条街上。

en: From the Ohashi Library to the Imperial Library was a distance of roughly one and a half ri.
u.src: 从大桥图书馆到帝国图书馆，两者相距约莫一里半的路程。

en: His first impression of the Imperial Library was vivid: he was afraid of the high ceiling, afraid of the tall windows, and afraid of the countless readers filling the countless chairs.
u.src: 他对帝国图书馆的第一印象很深——他害怕挑高的天花板，害怕高大的窗子，害怕坐满无数椅子的无数看书人。

en: Fortunately, after he had gone there two or three times, that fear gradually disappeared.
u.src: 但是，幸亏在去了两三次后，这种害怕就逐渐消失了。

en: Before long, he began to feel affection for the reading room, the iron ladders, the card cabinets, and the basement cafeteria.
u.src: 很快，他就对阅览室、铁梯子、书卡柜子、地下食堂有了亲切感受。

en: Later, he also came to use the school libraries of universities and high schools.
u.src: 后来，他也会使用大学和高中的学校图书馆。

en: Among the hundreds of books, there were several dozen that he liked best, but...
u.src: 在数百本书籍里，他最喜欢的有几十本书，但是——

en: But what he liked best were still the books he had bought himself; no matter what their contents were like, he loved those books.
u.src: 但是，他最喜欢的还是自己所购买的书，无论内容怎么样，他都是喜欢这些书。

en: In order to buy books, Shinsuke never set foot in coffeehouses.
u.src: 为了买书，信辅从不踏足咖啡厅。

en: But his pocket money was never enough.
u.src: 但是，他的零用钱总是不够用。

en: Because of this, every Wednesday he had to go to a relative's house and tutor middle school students in mathematics.
u.src: 为此，他每周三都不得不去亲戚家教中学生数学。

en: Even so, there were still times when he ran short of money, and then he had no choice but to sell his books.
u.src: 即便这样，钱还是有不够用的时候，他就不得不的采用卖书的办法了。

en: But the price he got for selling a book was not even half of what he had paid for it.
u.src: 但是，卖书的价格连买书价格的一半都没有。

en: And that was not all: to sell books he had treasured for years to a secondhand bookshop was, for him, nothing short of a tragedy.
u.src: 不仅仅是这样，把常年珍藏的图书卖给旧书店，这种事对他来说简直是个悲剧。

en: Once, on a night when a light snow was falling, he went to Jimbocho and browsed one secondhand bookshop after another.
u.src: 曾经，他在某个下小雪的夜晚，到神保町一家又一家逛旧书店。

ja: ツァラトゥストラはかく
en: In one of those secondhand bookshops, he saw a copy of Thus Spoke Zarathustra.
u.src: 他在其中某家旧书店看到了一本《查拉图斯特拉如是说》。

ja: の『ツァラトゥストラはかく
en: It was not an ordinary copy of Thus Spoke Zarathustra; it was the very copy, marked with his own handwriting, that he had sold just over two months earlier.
u.src: 那不是一本普通的《查拉图斯特拉如是说》，那是两个多月前他才卖掉的那本沾有自己手迹的《查拉图斯特拉如是说》。

en: Standing there in the bookshop, he read that copy of Thus Spoke Zarathustra once more, and the more he read, the harder it was to part with it.
u.src: 他站在书店里，又读了一遍那本《查拉图斯特拉如是说》，越看越舍不得。
“这本书多少钱？”

en: After standing there for ten-some minutes, he took Thus Spoke Zarathustra and asked the bookstore owner's wife.
u.src: 站了十几分钟，他拿着《查拉图斯特拉如是说》问书店老板娘。

en: One yen and sixty sen. I will make it a little cheaper for you!
u.src: “一圆六十钱，给你便宜一点吧！

en: One yen and fifty sen will do.
u.src: 一圆五十钱就可以了。”

en: Shinsuke remembered clearly that at the time he had sold this book for only seventy sen.
u.src: 信辅清楚的记得，当时他这本书只卖了七十钱。

en: After bargaining for a long time, he finally managed to buy the book back for one yen and forty sen, exactly twice what he had sold it for then.
u.src: 讨价还价半天，好不容易才以一圆四十钱，也就是当时卖价的两倍，最后把书又买了回来。

en: On that snowy night, both the houses lining the street and the streetcars passing along the road seemed filled with a subtle stillness.
u.src: 下雪的的夜晚，不管时候街道两边的住户，还是路上开过的电车，都有种微妙的寂静感。

ja: の『ツァラトゥストラはかく
en: As he walked through the streets on the long way back to Honjo, he kept thinking now and then of the iron-gray covered copy of Thus Spoke Zarathustra tucked inside his coat.
u.src: 他走过街道，回到很远的本所路上，不时记挂着怀里的那本铁灰色封面的《查拉图斯特拉如是说》。

en: At the same time, he could not help mocking himself under his breath again...
u.src: 与此同时，他嘴里又不由的嘲笑自己……
六 朋友

en: Shinsuke's principle in making friends was that the other person had to possess talent.
u.src: 信辅交朋友的原则是对方必须有才能。

en: Even a morally upright gentleman, if he had no talent beyond his character, was to him no more than a useless passerby.
u.src: 就算是品行端正的君子，如果除了品性之外没什么才能，对他来说都是没用的路人。

ja: からかわずにいられなかった。
en: No, rather, whenever he met them, he naturally showed this attitude, and even could not help mocking these clowns.
u.src: 不，毋宁说每次见到他们，他都自然的表现这种态度，甚至不得不揶揄这些丑角。

en: With only six points for conduct, he moved from middle school to high school and from high school to university, and at each stage of school life he was always unable to keep from laughing at such people.
u.src: 操行分只有六分的他，从初中到高中，从高中到大学，在几个阶段的学校生活里，他总是不由的嘲笑那种人。

en: Among them, of course, there were some who grew angry at this ridicule.
u.src: 他们之中当然有人对这种嘲笑感到愤怒。

en: However, there were also some who maintained the attitude of proper gentlemen toward this ridicule from beginning to end.
u.src: 不过，也有人对这种嘲笑始终保持正人君子的态度。

en: He even felt more or less pleased at being called an unpleasant person.
u.src: 对于自己被称为“令人讨厌的人”，他还多多少少感觉开心。

ja: てずにはいられなかった。
en: But when no matter how he mocked the other person he received no response at all, he could not help becoming angry.
u.src: 可是，不管怎么嘲讽对方，却得不到任何回应，他就不得不愤怒了。

en: In fact, there had once been such a gentleman: a humanities classmate from high school, an admirer of Livingstone.
u.src: 其实，曾经有过这样一个君子——高中时候的一个文科同学，一个利文斯通的崇拜者。

en: When Shinsuke was living in the same school building as him, he once casually told him that even Byron, after reading Livingstone's biography, was so moved that his face was covered with tears.
u.src: 信辅在跟他住同一间校舍的时候，曾经信口开河的对他说，连拜伦读了利文斯通的传记之后，也感动的流泪满面。

en: Twenty years had already passed since then, and that admirer of Livingstone was still praising Livingstone in the bulletin of a certain Christian church.
u.src: 从那个时候开始，到现在已经过去了二十年了，那个利文斯通的崇拜者在某基督教会机关志上，还在歌颂斯文利通。

en: Not only that, but at the beginning of the article there was also a passage like this: Even the demonic poet Byron read Livingstone's biography and was moved to tears; what does this make us think of?
u.src: 不仅仅是这样，文章的开头还有这样一段话：“连恶魔诗人拜伦读了利文斯通的传记也感动的泪流满面，这让我们想到了什么呢？”

en: Shinsuke's principle in making friends was that the other person had to have talent.
u.src: 信辅交朋友的原则是对方必须有才能。

en: Even a morally upright gentleman, if he had no intense pursuit of knowledge, was to him nothing more than a useless passerby.
u.src: 就算是品行端正的君子，如果对知识没有强烈的追求，对他来说都是没用的路人。

en: He did not require his friends to be gentle and kind by nature.
u.src: 他不要求朋友性情温和善良。

en: Even if his friends lacked the passion of youth, he did not mind.
u.src: 即使他的朋友没有青年人的热情，他也觉得无所谓。

en: No, rather, so-called good friends made him feel afraid.
u.src: 不，不如说所谓的好朋友让他觉得害怕。

ja: っていなければならなかった
en: Therefore, all of his friends had to have intellect.
u.src: 所以，他的朋友都一定得有头脑。
头脑——一颗清晰的的头脑。

en: He preferred people with clear minds to beautiful youths.
u.src: 他喜欢头脑清晰的人胜过美少年。

en: At the same time, he hated people with clear minds more than morally upright gentlemen.
u.src: 与此同时，他憎恶头脑清楚的人胜过品行端正的君子。

en: In fact, his friendships were often mixed with hatred within the passion of affection.
u.src: 事实上，他的友情常常都是在喜欢的热情里，掺杂这憎恶。

en: Even now, Shinsuke still felt that there was no friendship outside such passion.
u.src: 直到现在，信辅依然觉得在这种热情之外没有友情。

en: He felt that, at least outside such passion, there was no friendship without the odor of Herr und Knecht, German for a master-servant relationship.
u.src: 他觉得至少在这种热情之外，没有不 Herr und Knecht（德语，直译为主仆关系）气味的友情。

en: Moreover, his friends at the time were, in another sense, enemies utterly opposed to him.
u.src: 况且他当时的朋友，从另一个方面说，正是与他势不两立的敌人。

en: He used his own mind as a weapon and fought them constantly.
u.src: 他用自己的头脑当做武器，不断跟他们做斗争。

en: Whitman, free verse, creative evolution, the battlefield was everywhere.
u.src: 惠特曼、自由诗、创造的进化——战场无处不在。

en: On that battlefield, he defeated his friends, or was defeated by them.
u.src: 在战场上，他打败他的朋友们，或者被他的朋友们打败。

en: This spiritual combat undoubtedly became for him an act of finding joy through slaughter.
u.src: 这种精神上的战斗，毫无疑问成为了他通过杀戮获得喜悦的行为。

en: Yet it was also an undeniable fact that new ideas and new images of beauty naturally emerged in the process.
u.src: 然而，在这个过程里自然展现的新观念和新的美感形象也是毫无疑问的事实。

en: How did the candlelight at three in the morning shine upon their debates?
u.src: 凌晨三点的烛光是怎样照耀他们的辩论的？

en: And how did the works of Saneatsu Mushanokoji dominate their arguments?
u.src: 武者小路实笃的作品又是怎样支配他们的论战的？

en: Shinsuke still clearly remembered one night in September when several large moths rushed toward the burning candle, and those dazzling moths suddenly appeared in the darkness.
u.src: 信辅还清楚的记得，在九月的某一个夜晚，有几只很大的飞蛾扑向了燃烧的蜡烛，绚丽夺目的飞蛾在黑夜中突然出现。

en: But once the moths flew into the flame, they died in an unbelievably instant moment.
u.src: 但是，一旦飞蛾扑火，也就不可思议的瞬间死去了。

ja: ではなかったのだろう
en: Perhaps this, too, was nothing very important.
u.src: 可能这也不是什么大不了的事。

en: But even today, whenever Shinsuke recalls this small incident, whenever he recalls the life and death of those mysteriously beautiful moths, somehow the depths of his heart are taken over by loneliness...
u.src: 但是，信辅一直到今天，只要一想起这件小事——只要一想起那不可思议的美丽飞蛾的生死，不知道怎么回事，他的内心深处就会被孤寂占领……

en: Shinsuke's principle in making friends was that the other person had to possess talent.
u.src: 信辅交朋友的原则是对方必须有才能。

ja: ただそれだけにすぎなかった
en: That was the only standard he had.
u.src: 标准也就只有这个罢了。

ja: がないわけではなかった
en: However, even that standard was not without exceptions.
u.src: 不过，那个标准也不是没有例外的时候。

en: The exception was the class difference that severed the friendship between him and his friends.
u.src: 那就是切断他和朋友之间友情的阶级差别。

en: Between Shinsuke and middle-class young men who had grown up in the same environment as he had, there was no barrier at all.
u.src: 信辅跟和他生长环境相同的中产阶级青年中间，没有任何隔阂。

en: But toward upper-class young men unfamiliar to him, and sometimes even toward young men of the upper middle class, he felt an unbelievable hatred, as though they were complete strangers.
u.src: 但是，跟和他不熟悉的上流阶级青年，有时候也会对中流上层阶级的青年，产生像陌生人一样的难以置信的憎恨干。

en: Among these people, some were lazy by nature, some were cowardly by nature, and some were lustful and self-indulgent.
u.src: 这些人当中，有些人生性懒惰，有些人生性怯懦，有些人好色纵欲。

ja: だけからではなかった
en: But he did not hate them solely for those reasons.
u.src: 但是，他不仅仅是因为这些原因憎恶他们。

en: No, rather, he hated their vague, indifferent attitude, that inexplicable air of meaninglessness.
u.src: 不，毋宁说是憎恨他们那种不知所谓的漠然态度。

en: In truth, what he hated most was that indescribable meaninglessness of theirs, which they themselves did not even notice.
u.src: 其实，他最憎恨的还是他们自己也没意识到的那种说不清的“不知所谓”。

en: Precisely because of this, he had an almost pathological concern for the lower classes, the people opposite to their class.
u.src: 正是因为这样，他对下层阶级——跟他们阶级相反的人群，有种几乎病态的关怀。

en: Shinsuke was filled with sympathy for them.
u.src: 信辅对他们充满同情。

en: Of course, this sympathy was of no use at all.
u.src: 当然，这种同情毫无用处。

en: Every time he shook hands with those people of indescribable meaninglessness, he felt as if needles were pricking his hand.
u.src: 每次跟那些说不清的“不知所谓”的人握手的时候，他都觉得如针刺手。

en: He remembered one afternoon in April, when a bitter cold wind was blowing, Shinsuke, still a high school student then, stood on the cliffs of Enoshima with a classmate, the eldest son of a baronial family.
u.src: 记得在四月的某个午后，寒风凛冽，当时还在上高中的信辅和他的同学——一位男爵家的长子，一起伫立在江之岛的断崖之上。

en: Below their feet lay a coastline of surging waves.
u.src: 脚下就是波涛汹涌的海岸线。

en: They threw a few copper coins into the sea and made several boys dive down to retrieve them.
u.src: 他们往海里扔几个铜板，让几个少年“潜水”去捞。

en: Whenever the copper coins fell into the sea, the boys jumped in one after another with splashes of plop, plop.
u.src: 每当铜板落入海中，少年就相继“扑通，扑通……”的跳进海里。

en: Yet one ama stood below the cliff before a fire burning dried seaweed, smiling as she gazed out over the surface of the sea.
u.src: 然而，有一个海女站在断崖下焚烧干海草的火堆前，笑着眺望海面。

en: This time, let us have that ama diver jump in too.
u.src: “这回让那个海女也一起跳进去吧。”

en: Shinsuke's friend wrapped a copper coin in the silver paper from a cigarette box, then suddenly spun around and threw the coin as hard as he could.
u.src: 信辅的朋友用香烟盒里的银色纸包着一枚铜币，然后猛一转身用力把铜币扔了出去。

en: The copper coin glittered and fell into the stormy sea.
u.src: 铜币闪闪发光，掉进了波涛汹涌的大海里。

en: At that very instant, the diving woman leapt into the sea ahead of the others.
u.src: 就在那一刹那，海女抢先跳进了海里。

en: Even now, Shinsuke clearly remembers the cruel smile that appeared at the corners of his friend's mouth.
u.src: 信辅直到现在，还清楚的记得他的朋友的嘴角浮现出的残忍笑容。

en: His friend possessed an extraordinary talent for foreign languages.
u.src: 他的朋友拥有过人的外语才能。

en: But he also certainly had extraordinarily sharp canine teeth...
u.src: 但是，他也确实有过人的尖利的犬齿……

en: Note: this novel was originally planned to be three or four times as long as it is now.
u.src: 附记：这篇小说本来计划写成现在的三四倍长。

en: The material published this time naturally does not match the title The First Half of Daidoji Shinsuke's Life,
u.src: 这次所发表的内容，和《大导寺信辅的前半生》的题目自然不相符合，

en: but mainly because there was no other name that could replace it, I had no choice but to keep using this title.
u.src: 主要因为没有其他名称可以替代，不得不沿用这个题目。

en: If this story can be taken as one piece within The First Half of Daidoji Shinsuke's Life,
u.src: 如果能够把这篇小说当做《大导寺信辅的前半生》里面的一篇，
那就再好不过了。
作者 谨识

en: The figs by the roadside had already withered,
u.src: 路边的无花果已经枯萎，

en: Christ also seemed to have stopped breathing.
u.src: 基督好像也没有呼吸了。

en: We too had no choice but to rest,
u.src: 我们也不得不休息，

en: Even if one is standing before the stage curtain.
u.src: 即使身在舞台幕布前。

en: The stage curtain mentioned here was nothing more than some patched-up canvas.
u.src: （这里所说的舞台幕布只是一些满是补丁的画布。）

en: But I am not world-weary like this poet.
u.src: 但是我并不像这位诗人一样厌世。

en: If only the kappa would be willing to come and see me from time to time...
u.src: 只要河童们愿意常常来看望一下我……

en: Oh yes, I forgot to mention it. You remember my judge friend, the kappa Peppu, don't you?
u.src: 对了，我忘记说了，你还记得我那位审判官朋友——河童培卟吧？

en: After he lost his job, he truly went mad.
u.src: 他失业后，真的发疯了。

en: They say he is now living in a mental hospital in the land of the kappa.
u.src: 据说现在正住在河童国的精神病院里。

en: If Dr. S agrees, I would very much like to go and visit him...
u.src: 倘若S博士同意的话，我很想去探望他呢……
